You are an agent who can operate an Android phone on behalf of a user. Based on user's goal/request, you may
- Answer back if the request/goal is a question (or a chat message), like user asks "What is my schedule for today?".
- Complete some tasks described in the requests/goals by performing actions (step by step) on the phone.

When given a user request, you will try to complete it step by step. At each step, a list of descriptions for most UI elements on the current screen will be given to you (each element can be specified by an index), together with a history of what you have done in previous steps. Based on these pieces of information and the goal, you must choose to perform one of the action in the following list (action description followed by the JSON format) by outputing the action in the correct JSON format.
- If you think the task has been completed, finish the task by using the status action with complete as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "complete"}`
- If you think the task is not feasible (including cases like you don't have enough information or can not perform some necessary actions), finish by using the `status` action with infeasible as goal_status: `{"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "infeasible"}`
- Answer user's question: `{"action_type": "answer", "text": "<answer_text>"}`
- Click/tap on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "click", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Long press on a UI element (specified by its index) on the screen: `{"action_type": "long_press", "index": <target_index>}`.
- Type text into an editable text field (specified by its index), this action contains clicking the text field, typing in the text and pressing the enter, so no need to click on the target field to start: `{"action_type": "input_text", "text": <text_input>, "index": <target_index>}`
- Press the Enter key: `{"action_type": "keyboard_enter"}`
- Navigate to the home screen: `{"action_type": "navigate_home"}`
- Navigate back: `{"action_type": "navigate_back"}`
- Scroll the screen or a scrollable UI element in one of the four directions, use the same numeric index as above if you want to scroll a specific UI element, leave it empty when scroll the whole screen: `{"action_type": "scroll", "direction": <up, down, left, right>, "index": <optional_target_index>}`
- Open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed): `{"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": <name>}`
- Wait for the screen to update: `{"action_type": "wait"}`

The current user goal/request is: Delete all but one of any recipes in the Broccoli app that are exact duplicates, ensuring at least one instance of each unique recipe remains

Here is a history of what you have done so far:
Step 1: Action selected: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Broccoli"}. Opened Broccoli app successfully; now viewing "All recipes" list with visible duplicates (e.g., multiple "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" entries with varying descriptions).
Step 2: Action selected: {"action_type": "long_press", "index": 16}. Long-pressed on "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" hoping for a delete context menu, but it opened the recipe detail view instead—no delete option appeared from the list. Need to try other methods (e.g., three-dot menu inside a recipe, swipe, or multi-select).
Step 3: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Opened the "More options" menu on the recipe detail screen, revealing the "Delete" option alongside "Share", "Share as file", and "Edit".
Step 4: Action selected: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}. The overflow menu was dismissed, returning to the recipe detail screen for "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" (still not back to the list). Next, navigate back again to reach the recipe list to identify duplicates.
Step 5: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 4}. Clicked the "Navigate up" button to return to the recipe list, where multiple Chicken Alfredo Pasta entries (some duplicates with different descriptions) and other recipes are now visible, ready for duplicate identification.
Step 6: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down on the recipe list; revealed new recipes (Eggplant Parmesan, Grilled Cheese with Tomato and Basil, Pan-Seared Salmon with Quinoa) not visible before, confirming the scroll worked.
Step 7: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 15}. Opened the duplicate "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" recipe detail via its card title; the detail screen now shows with a "More options" (overflow) menu accessible for deletion.
Step 8: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Opened the overflow menu for "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" by tapping "More options", revealing the Delete option to proceed with removing the duplicate.
Step 9: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Tapped "Delete" in the overflow menu for a duplicate "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" recipe, bringing up the "Delete this recipe?" confirmation dialog. Next: confirm deletion by tapping DELETE.
Step 10: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 2}. Confirmed deletion of a duplicate recipe by tapping DELETE on the dialog; dialog dismissed, list now shows two "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" entries still present, so duplicates remain and need further cleanup.
Step 11: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "up", "index": 4}. Scrolled up in recipe list to reveal the topmost item; discovered it's "Baked Cod with Lemon and Dill", and now multiple "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" duplicates are fully visible for removal.
Step 12: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 28}. Tapped on the bottom duplicate "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" to open its detail view (intending to delete this instance). Successfully opened the recipe; next step is to find and use the delete option.
Step 13: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 6}. Tapped "More options" on the "Chicken Alfredo Pasta" recipe detail screen, which opened a menu with Share, Share as file, Edit, and Delete options.
Step 14: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}. Clicked "Delete" in the recipe overflow menu; a confirmation dialog "Delete this recipe?" with CANCEL and DELETE buttons appeared, ready to confirm deletion.
Step 15: Output for action selection is not in the correct format, so no action is performed.
Step 16: Action selected: {"action_type": "click", "index": 2}. Tapped DELETE on the confirmation dialog to remove a duplicate recipe; the dialog closed and the recipe list is now displayed with remaining recipes.
Step 17: Action selected: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down", "index": 4}. Scrolled down the recipe list successfully; previously visible Chicken Alfredo Pasta duplicates moved off-screen, now displaying new recipes (Eggplant Parmesan, Grilled Cheese with Tomato and Basil, Pan-Seared Salmon with Quinoa, Thai Peanut Noodle Salad), all appear unique. Continue scrolling to check entire list for duplicates of any recipe.
